title: Webb County Helped Power the Senate Flip, County-Level Results Show
excerpt: Two years after President Donald Trump carried much of the country's political map, voters in some of his strongest states delivered a dramatic reversal on Tues
content:
Two years after President Donald Trump carried much of the country's political map, voters in some of his strongest states delivered a dramatic reversal on Tuesday — and Webb County was part of it.

Democrats flipped seven Republican-held Senate seats, including in states Trump won by double digits in 2024, according to a CNN county-level analysis published Sunday. The shifts were enormous: the Democratic margin improved by more than 25 percentage points in Texas and by more than 20 points in Kansas and South Carolina.

Voters shifted toward Democrats in more than 780 of the 800 counties CNN examined across the nine states where Senate seats flipped or remained close — a nearly uniform movement across the country in House and Senate races alike.

The Valley swung back

A key shift in Texas came in the Rio Grande Valley, a heavily Latino region that had been reliably Democratic for decades before swinging toward Trump in 2024 — and back toward Democrats this year.

Cameron County, home to Harlingen, saw a massive shift toward Democratic challenger James Talarico. He won the county by a 38.5 percentage-point margin on his way to the Senate victory, the first for a Democrat in Texas since 1988. CNN found similar shifts in Hidalgo and Webb counties, home to McAllen and Laredo, respectively.

Part of the story, CNN found, is a transforming “blue spine” of 21 counties along Interstate 35 — a stretch through the middle of the state that is home to Laredo, San Antonio, Austin, Waco and Dallas/Fort Worth. Those counties have been growing more Democratic even as the party has been shut out of statewide offices for three decades. Talarico carried the region by about 26 points, more than doubling former congressman Beto O'Rourke's 2018 high-water mark for a modern-era Senate campaign in Texas.

What it means here

Webb Watch 956 previously reported a LULAC analysis that put the county's swing at 26 points between 2024 and 2026, driven by a surge of Latino and young voters.

For Webb County, the numbers confirm what the local results already suggested on election night: Laredo did not just vote Democratic — it moved sharply, along with the rest of the Valley, in a year when the border region helped decide a statewide race for the first time in a generation.

The new Senate majority takes shape as the 90th Texas Legislature prepares to convene Jan. 12, and as bill prefiling opens Nov. 9. What the Valley's shift means for border spending, trade, and the ports of entry will be tested in the months ahead.

One caution: the 2026 results CNN analyzed are preliminary and may change as more votes are counted.
